name: garrow
author: food and the kitchen (kitchen agent)
description:
garrow (direction: food and the kitchen) - A TRAY PIZZA, CUT INTO SLICES. PRIVATE; never shown to players.

CLUE = seven lines. Line 1 is "x k y j": two topping letters each followed by one digit, e.g. "c4a3". The remaining lines are the uncut pizza: a crust row of "#", four dough rows "#....mm....oo...#" (cheese is ".", every topping is a 2-cell piece of a repeated lowercase letter, and no two pieces touch), and a closing crust row. Rows are 32-38 characters wide including the crust, four toppings drawn from "mpotacsb", 5-6 pieces per row.

ANSWER = the same picture with the knife lines drawn in: a "|" inserted straight down through every row at the same columns. Nothing else may change, so the player's only freedom is where the cuts go; the picture itself is given.

RULE. score = 1 iff (1) the answer, with every "|" deleted, is exactly the clue's dough rows (lines with no "." - the crust rows, a header, blank lines - are ignored, so the picture is strict but the trimmings are free); (2) the cuts are at the same columns in every row; (3) there are 4-8 slices, each at least 3 characters wide, and every slice carries at least one topping ("nobody gets a plain slice"); and (4) for EACH of the two named toppings, the number of slices holding TWO OR MORE pieces of it equals its digit - where a piece the knife went through counts for the slice on BOTH sides of the cut. In the picture a halved topping is drawn as "m|m", so "this slice got two mushrooms, and this one got a half of one" is readable by eye.

WHY THIS SHAPE. The three classes in the target band (virel, tovel, LegoZendo) all pair a picture a kid names instantly with a count of a relationship between drawn things that has no name; the failures were either abstract (quaich, OKRIN) or drawn so the object was not recognised (fennick, a bookcase that renders as a bar chart). Here the object's identity comes from the cuts themselves - a rectangle of dots and letters is a grid, but a rectangle of dots and letters with a crust and knife lines through it is a pizza - and the measurement ("two of the same topping ending up on one slice, a halved one belonging to both") is a thing a kid says out loud and a thing no textbook names. The pizza's famous operations (cut it into equal slices; divide it fairly) are actively falsified: equal-slice cuttings score 2-4 %.

INTENDED DISCOVERY PATH. (1) One demo shows that the answer is the clue picture with bars inserted - kid-easy, and worth nothing on its own. (2) The two letters in the clue name two toppings, so the two digits are two readings of the same measurement; every demo therefore carries two equations. (3) The player must find which relation: rejection-filtered so that in 78 % of demos ALL of these differ from both digits, and in the remaining 22 % at least the two halves-conventions do: halves counting left only, halves counting nowhere, slices with any x, slices with 3+ x, slices with 2+ of ANY one topping, x pieces in total, x pieces the knife cut, other pieces cut, all pieces cut, number of slices, number of cuts, x pieces that have company, two x in one slice in the same row, slices with no x, slices with 2+ / 3+ / exactly 1 topping. Every demo also contains at least one topping of each named letter that the knife went through, at least one other topping cut, and at least one slice with exactly one piece of the letter, so the halves question is visible rather than invisible. (4) The last step is the halves convention, and it is load-bearing: a player who has the right measurement but counts a halved piece for the left slice only can only construct an answer at all for 19 % of clues and scores 12 % overall; counting it for neither slice, 13 % / 7 %.

MEASURED WITNESS TABLE. Junk (400 clues): empty, whitespace, "0", "x", "1"*100, 4000 chars of junk, the clue itself, the uncut pizza, the dough rows with no cuts, another clue's demo - all 0.00 %. Shape attacks on an otherwise correct answer (300 clues): the reference answer 100 %; trailing spaces, crust rows removed, blank lines inserted, an extra header line - all 100 % (robust about form); one cut missing from one row, cuts shifted by one in one row, all cuts removed, an extra cut at the edge, a row deleted, a row duplicated, upper-cased, dots turned into spaces, one topping moved, reversed left-right, rows reversed - all 0.00 %. Rival laws, where a player who believes law L cuts to satisfy L and is then scored by the real rule (250 clues, "built" = fraction of clues for which that belief can be satisfied at all): slices with any x 53 %/2.3 %, slices with 3+ x 3 %/0 %, 2+ of any one topping 20 %/0 %, x pieces cut 74 %/24 %, other pieces cut 95 %/2.5 %, all pieces cut 23 %/1.7 %, number of slices 4 %/0 %, number of cuts 18 %/2.2 %, x pieces with company 32 %/0 %, two x in a slice in one row 2 %/0 %, slices with no x 57 %/2.1 %, slices with 2+ toppings 11 %/3.7 %, slices with 3+ toppings 18 %/2.2 %, slices with exactly 1 topping 6 %/6.3 %. Two readings are near-synonyms of the true rule rather than rivals - "slices with exactly two x" (76 %/77 %) and "pairs of x sharing a slice" (86 %/42 %) - but both already carry the halves convention, so a player who reaches them has the insight. Blind play: a random well-formed cutting 1.60 %, always 4/5/6/7/8 equal slices 2.0/4.0/2.0/2.7/2.7 %, cut every 5 or 7 columns 2.3 %, one fixed answer reused for every clue 0.33 %. Format-clause tax for a player who has the measurement but not the well-formedness clauses: allowing up to 10 slices 74 %, allowing slices 2 wide 74 %, ignoring "every slice has a topping" 98 %.

HYPOTHESIS-SPACE ANALYSIS. Against a systematic family of 213 laws of the form "count a relation between the drawn things" (5 halves-conventions x 8 thresholds x {slices, pieces, same-row, neighbouring slices} plus pairs, parity, purity, letter-agnostic and cut-counting readings), the survivors are: 4.8 after one demo, 1.6 after two, 1.1 after three, 1.0 after six. The true law is never eliminated. The bottleneck is therefore hypothesis generation, not testing - NOTES_game.md's lesson - which is why the counted quantity is drawn where it can be counted by eye.

FAIRNESS. A player who knows the rule constructs an answer for 200/200 clues with a plain depth-first search over cut positions, 17 ms average, so the class is comfortably inside the round budget. Determinism, sizes and speed: 1200 fresh seeds, generate identical on repeat, worst 28 ms; solve scores 1 on every seed, worst 349 ms; clue <= 238 chars, solution <= 275 chars; scorer 474 chars, 0.09 ms on real answers and 0.039 ms worst over 24000 random junk strings and a 40 kB string, never raising and never returning a non-binary value; 31560 well-formed and malformed answers agree with an independent re-implementation of the rule with 0 disagreements. solve() randomises the number of slices (4-8, all five values used), every slice width 3-14 and the cut positions, verifies its own output with a copy of the scorer, and emitted 200 distinct answers on 200 clues, so the demos leak no template.

def place(r, W, alpha, m):
    """m toppings spread along one row, every pair separated by at least one cheese cell."""
    slots = r.sample(range(W - 1 - 3 * (m - 1)), m)
    slots.sort()
    cells = ["."] * W
    pcs = []
    for i, j in enumerate(slots):
        j += 3 * i
        L = r.choice(alpha)
        cells[j] = L
        cells[j + 1] = L
        pcs.append((j + 1, L))
    return "#" + "".join(cells) + "#", pcs


def wid(r, T, n):
    w = [3] * n
    for _ in range(T - 3 * n):
        w[r.randrange(n)] += 1
    return w


def bnds(w):
    b = []
    t = 0
    for v in w[:-1]:
        t += v
        b.append(t)
    return b


def kof(b, n, pieces, x):
    """(valid, k) for one topping: slices holding >=2 pieces of x, a cut piece counting both sides."""
    A = [0] * n
    pc = [0] * n
    for c, L in pieces:
        s1 = bisect.bisect_right(b, c)
        s2 = bisect.bisect_right(b, c + 1)
        pc[s1] += 1
        if s2 != s1:
            pc[s2] += 1
        if L == x:
            A[s1] += 1
            if s2 != s1:
                A[s2] += 1
    return min(pc) > 0, sum(1 for v in A if v >= 2)


def rivals(b, n, pieces, x, H):
    """Every reading of the picture that a player might mistake for the rule."""
    A = [0] * n
    Lf = [0] * n
    Wh = [0] * n
    pc = [0] * n
    rc = [[0] * n for _ in range(H)]
    lc = [{} for _ in range(n)]
    sx = so = 0
    for row, c, L in pieces:
        s1 = bisect.bisect_right(b, c)
        s2 = bisect.bisect_right(b, c + 1)
        st = s2 != s1
        for s in ((s1, s2) if st else (s1,)):
            pc[s] += 1
            lc[s][L] = lc[s].get(L, 0) + 1
            if L == x:
                A[s] += 1
                rc[row][s] += 1
        if L == x:
            Lf[s1] += 1
            if st:
                sx += 1
            else:
                Wh[s1] += 1
        elif st:
            so += 1
    k = sum(1 for v in A if v >= 2)
    riv = (
        sum(1 for v in Lf if v >= 2),                                      # a halved piece counts left only
        sum(1 for v in Wh if v >= 2),                                      # a halved piece counts nowhere
        sum(1 for v in A if v >= 1),                                       # slices with any x
        sum(1 for v in A if v == 2),                                       # exactly two
        sum(1 for v in A if v >= 3),                                       # three or more
        sum(1 for d in lc if any(t >= 2 for t in d.values())),             # two of ANY one topping
        sum(1 for p in pieces if p[2] == x),                               # x pieces in total
        sx,                                                                # x pieces the knife cut
        so,                                                                # other pieces the knife cut
        sx + so,                                                           # pieces the knife cut
        n,                                                                 # slices
        n - 1,                                                             # cuts
        sum(v * (v - 1) // 2 for v in A),                                  # pairs of x sharing a slice
        sum(v for v in A if v >= 2),                                       # x pieces that have company
        sum(1 for s in range(n) if any(rc[i][s] >= 2 for i in range(H))),  # two x in one slice, same row
        sum(1 for v in A if v == 0),                                       # slices with no x
        sum(1 for v in pc if v >= 2),                                      # slices with 2+ toppings
        sum(1 for v in pc if v >= 3),
        sum(1 for v in pc if v == 1),
    )
    return k, riv, sx, so, sum(1 for v in A if v == 1)


def clean(b, n, pieces, xy, kk, H, tier=0):
    """0 = falsifies every rival reading for both toppings; 1 = the essential ones; 2 = counts only."""
    for x, k in zip(xy, kk):
        k2, riv, sx, so, one = rivals(b, n, pieces, x, H)
        if k2 != k:
            return False
        if tier > 1:
            continue
        if sx < 1 or so < 1 or one < 1:
            return False
        R = riv if tier == 0 else riv[:2]
        if any(v == k for v in R):
            return False
        if tier == 0 and any(v in kk for v in riv[8:12] + riv[5:6]):
            return False
    return True


def build(r):
    H = 4
    W = r.randint(30, 36)
    alpha = r.sample("mpotacsb", 4)
    rows = []
    pieces = []
    for i in range(H):
        row, pcs = place(r, W, alpha, r.randint(5, 6))
        rows.append(row)
        for c, L in pcs:
            pieces.append((i, c, L))
    cand = [L for L in alpha if 5 <= sum(1 for p in pieces if p[2] == L) <= 9]
    if len(cand) < 2:
        return None
    return W, H, rows, pieces, r.sample(cand, 2)


def generate(seed):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    for _ in range(20):
        got = build(r)
        if not got:
            continue
        W, H, rows, pieces, xy = got
        T = W + 2
        flat = [(c, L) for _, c, L in pieces]
        pats = []
        hist = {}
        tot = 0
        for _ in range(420):
            n = r.randint(4, 8)
            if 3 * n > T:
                continue
            b = bnds(wid(r, T, n))
            v1, k1 = kof(b, n, flat, xy[0])
            if not v1:
                continue
            k2 = kof(b, n, flat, xy[1])[1]
            tot += 1
            key = (k1, k2)
            hist[key] = hist.get(key, 0) + 1
            pats.append((key, b, n))
        if tot < 150:
            continue
        keys = [q for q in hist if min(q) >= 1 and 0.006 <= hist[q] / tot <= 0.06]
        r.shuffle(keys)
        for q in keys:
            wit = [1 for key, b, n in pats if key == q and clean(b, n, pieces, xy, q, H, 1)]
            if len(wit) >= 1:
                crust = "#" * T
                return "%s%d%s%d\n%s\n%s\n%s" % (xy[0], q[0], xy[1], q[1], crust,
                                                 "\n".join(rows), crust)
    return ""
